re_line: Wong defends AUKUS alliance against Labor critics · Chalmers warns jobless rate to top 5 percent · COP31 collapses, Bowen under fire · Newspoll: Taylor overtakes Albanese · Luxon brands Putin 'a killer'
morning_memo: Wong defends the US alliance against Labor critics the same day Marles disputes a US Congressional Budget Office finding that AUKUS submarine production is 'flat.'
Chalmers warns unemployment will climb past five percent and flags net spending cuts ahead of December's mid-year budget, due after December 8.
Luxon calls Putin 'a killer, not a friend' after Trump's warm APEC encounter, as COP31 collapses in Antalya and Fiji pushes for a standalone ocean decision at the UN.

top_stories.headline: Wong tells Labor critics Australia cannot 'abandon' the US alliance
top_stories.body: **Penny Wong** will push back on Labor figures urging Australia to distance itself from Washington and abandon the AUKUS submarine pact, arguing the alliance remains essential despite turmoil under President Trump. The rebuttal lands the same day **Richard Marles** disputed a US Congressional Budget Office finding that submarine production is 'flat,' telling the ABC's Insiders that output is in fact increasing.
top_stories.src_line: per SMH (Matthew Knott): "Wong to Labor critics: Australians cannot ‘abandon the US’ despite Trump turmoil"

top_stories.headline: Chalmers flags spending cuts as jobless rate set to top five percent
top_stories.body: Treasurer **Jim Chalmers** told parliament the mid-year budget update, due after December 8, will show higher unemployment and inflation and slower growth, warning 2027 could get 'a bit harder' though he does not forecast a recession. He said planned savings are on track to 'more than cover' any new spending, calling the figures 'concerning.'
top_stories.src_line: per ABC News: "Jim Chalmers says he doesn't expect a recession, but 'things might get a bit harder'"

top_stories.headline: Albanese stands by Bowen as Coalition demands COP31 resignation
top_stories.body: **Anthony Albanese** defended Energy Minister **Chris Bowen** after UN climate talks in Antalya collapsed without a deal, the longest COP on record, blaming 'difficult geopolitical times.' Opposition MP **Dan Tehan** told question time Bowen had wasted '*$150 million* of our money on his big COP flop' and called for his resignation.
top_stories.src_line: per SMH (Natassia Chrysanthos): "Albanese stands by Bowen after failed COP amid global recriminations" · also Guardian Australia

top_stories.headline: Constitutional scholar brands defence sites bill 'lazy and irresponsible'
top_stories.body: Constitutional law expert **Anne Twomey** warned Labor's 'accelerating capability and protecting bases' bill, which lets government secretly designate special security zones around defence sites, raises serious legal issues, calling the lack of debate 'flabbergasting.' The bill is expected to pass parliament this week despite crossbench opposition; Albanese dismissed critics as 'jump[ing] at shadows.'
top_stories.src_line: per Guardian Australia (Josh Butler): "Constitutional law expert brands defence bill allowing secret security rules ‘lazy and irresponsible’"

overnight_items.headline: Wong to warn US-China rivalry is making the world more dangerous
overnight_items.body_text: **Penny Wong** will tell the Senate Tuesday that the US and China are 'increasingly willing to wield their power without regard for the rules' that have helped prevent major conflict for decades. 'Rules without power cannot secure peace. Power without rules cannot sustain it,' she will say, arguing Australia must build coalitions to protect its interests.

overnight_items.headline: Lowy Asia Power Index: US loses ground in Asia, China gains
overnight_items.body_text: The Lowy Institute's 2026 Asia Power Index found the gap between US and Chinese military capability in Asia is now the narrowest on record, a result authors **Hunter Marston** and Jack Sato attribute more to 'Washington's missteps' than Beijing's advances. China now leads the index's Economic Relationship and Diplomatic Influence measures, while Australia's comprehensive power dipped slightly.

overnight_items.headline: Trump administration scrutiny hits Canberra's news and tech rules
overnight_items.body_text: Politico reports the Trump administration has put Canberra's news bargaining rules and technology ambitions 'in the firing line,' adding friction to digital policy disputes between Washington and Canberra as parliament debates AI and platform regulation this week.

overnight_items.headline: Anthropic's Canberra lobbying operation grows to 46 lobbyists
overnight_items.body_text: Politico reports Anthropic now has *46 registered lobbyists* working Canberra, underscoring the scale of AI industry engagement as a joint parliamentary committee prepares to report this week on AI regulation, datacentres, and copyright.

pacific_wire.headline: Derelict cargo ship risks sinking in Majuro lagoon
pacific_wire.body_text: A US Coast Guard assessment of the *MV Futun Creek*, stranded in Majuro for nearly a year after arriving with multiple hull holes in January, found 'severe corrosion and structural failure' and says the vessel is unfit for ocean travel. The ship, carrying iron ore with roughly 30 seafarers aboard, poses a potential environmental and humanitarian threat if it sinks.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji navy officer says legislation alone 'cannot stop a coup'
pacific_wire.body_text: Lieutenant **Atunaisa Waqainabete** told a public consultation on the proposed RFMF Bill 2026 that the legislation, meant to make it harder for the military to stage a coup, requires culture and civilian leadership alongside legal reform. Major **Jone Lesivakarua** acknowledged the military 'can be used or have been used before to advance political interests.'

pacific_wire.headline: Guam's incoming legislature speaker vows fiscal discipline
pacific_wire.body_text: Senator **Chris Duenas**, selected as speaker of the incoming 39th Guam Legislature, pledged full implementation of performance-based budgeting as Republicans take control after narrowly winning the November 3 elections, eight seats to seven. Duenas chairs the finance committee and succeeds Speaker **Frank Blas Jr.**

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji seeks standalone ocean decision after COP31 text rejected
pacific_wire.body_text: Fiji is pushing for a standalone ocean decision at the United Nations after the COP31 cover text, which avoided any mention of fossil fuels, was rejected by the European Union and others, collapsing the longest climate summit on record.

pacific_wire.headline: Tuvalu, Nauru, and Vanuatu back Cuba against US blockade at UN
pacific_wire.body_text: Tuvalu Prime Minister **Feleti Teo** told the UN General Assembly the US embargo against Cuba 'contravenes the human-rights commitments of the United Nations,' while Nauru's President **David Adeang** and Vanuatu's UN ambassador **Odo Tevi** echoed calls to lift sanctions, continuing a pattern of Pacific solidarity with Havana.

new_zealand.headline: New Zealand says it would have backed the collapsed COP31 deal
new_zealand.body_text: A spokesperson for caretaker climate minister **Simon Watts** said New Zealand was 'ready to support consensus in the room' on the COP31 cover decision that the European Union and others rejected for omitting any mention of fossil fuels. Green MP **Francisco Hernandez** called the lack of fossil fuel language 'the most egregious thing.'

new_zealand.headline: Luxon calls Putin 'a killer, not a friend' after Trump's APEC embrace
new_zealand.body_text: Caretaker Prime Minister **Christopher Luxon** said he told Vladimir Putin directly at APEC in China that the war in Ukraine was 'illegal, unprovoked, unjustifiable,' rejecting Trump's description of Putin as 'my friend.' Luxon said Putin launched missiles into Kyiv civilian buildings within days of the summit, killing a 10 year old boy and a 20 year old health worker.

new_zealand.headline: Luxon says pay equity settlement is a matter for the next government
new_zealand.body_text: Caretaker Prime Minister **Christopher Luxon** said decisions on pay equity will be left to the next government, as teacher aides rallied in Wellington demanding action on stalled pay claims.

china_in_the_pacific.headline: Russian and Chinese firms eye Timor-Leste's Greater Sunrise after Woodside exit
china_in_the_pacific.body_text: Timor-Leste says Russian and Chinese companies have expressed interest in the Greater Sunrise gas project after Woodside sold back its *33.4 percent* stake last month. Analyst **Saul Kavonic** said the government's insistence on proceeding risks either bankrupting the country or forcing it to 'cede its economic sovereignty' to a country such as China.

canberra_politics.headline: Newspoll: Taylor overtakes Albanese, Labor ties One Nation on primary vote
canberra_politics.body_text: A Newspoll published in The Australian found *42 percent* of voters now prefer **Angus Taylor** as prime minister, overtaking **Anthony Albanese**, whose net approval rating fell to a record low of minus 31. Labor's primary vote is now tied with One Nation at 27 percent, with voters citing economic difficulties and public gaffes.

canberra_politics.headline: Plibersek accuses Coalition and One Nation of enabling online harm
canberra_politics.body_text: **Tanya Plibersek** used a question time speech to attack opponents of the government's digital duty of care, saying they were allowing young people to be exposed to harm, as parliament works through its final sitting week of 2026.

canberra_politics.headline: Jewish body warns against stripping religion from terrorism definition
canberra_politics.body_text: Australia's peak Jewish body told **Anthony Albanese** that removing religion from the legal definition of terrorism would be a 'dangerous distraction,' as the government considers changes to counter-terrorism law.

canberra_politics.headline: Survey finds seven in ten MPs say politics damaged their wellbeing
canberra_politics.body_text: New research found *seven in ten* Australian MPs say holding public office has damaged their wellbeing, with one in five reporting suicidal thoughts. Independent **Helen Haines** said politicians 'shouldn't have to wear a flak jacket' to do the job.

business_economy.headline: Grattan Institute urges Australia to cut reliance on imported fuel
business_economy.body_text: A Grattan Institute report calls for capping diesel tax credits for big business, building 'clean' refineries, and targeting EV subsidies to less wealthy households, warning Australia imports too much fuel and must brace for supply shocks like those from the Iran war.

business_economy.headline: RBA modelling finds Labor's CGT changes could stoke inflation
business_economy.body_text: Reserve Bank research suggests the overhaul of capital gains tax concessions may drive wealthier households to spend more and stoke business uncertainty, according to the Australian Financial Review, adding a fresh complication to the government's inflation fight.

business_economy.headline: New Zealand dollar slumps to 17-year low against the US dollar
business_economy.body_text: The New Zealand dollar has fallen to its lowest level since the 2009 financial crisis, trading around *0.5467* against the US dollar. BNZ strategist **Jason Wong** said a weak Reserve Bank rate stance has recently given way to a broader global risk-off mood tied to AI-sector jitters on Wall Street.

calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Digital duty of care, gas reservation, and the contested defence sites security bill are all expected to be forced through before the summer break.
A poor result would compound pressure on federal Labor, whose Newspoll ratings have fallen to new lows.
Chalmers has flagged net spending cuts alongside higher unemployment and inflation forecasts, a signal for fiscal settings heading into 2027.

calendar_watch.event: Latest possible date for the next Australian federal election
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Newspoll now shows Angus Taylor leading Albanese as preferred prime minister, intensifying pressure on Labor's term.

key_stat.label: Albanese's net Newspoll approval rating, a record low
key_stat.context: Angus Taylor now leads as preferred prime minister at 42 percent and Labor's primary vote is tied with One Nation at 27 percent.

also_today.headline: How Pacific Islands are right-sizing Chinese policing
also_today.body_text: The Lowy Institute's Interpreter argues Pacific governments' own agency, not external pressure, is making it harder for Beijing to sustain a long-term policing presence in the region.

also_today.headline: Former Fiji deputy PM calls for a visa-free Pacific and ANZ economic integration
also_today.body_text: Former Fiji deputy prime minister **Biman Prasad** argues for going beyond the Vuvale Union toward a visa-free Pacific and a Fiji-Australia economic partnership modelled on the Australia-New Zealand Closer Economic Relations agreement.

also_today.headline: Fiji's G11 bloc applies to contest election under People's Alliance
also_today.body_text: Members of Fiji's Group of 11 lodged individual applications to contest the next general election under Prime Minister **Sitiveni Rabuka**'s People's Alliance, despite uncertainty over whether formally joining a party could affect their current parliamentary seats.
